newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Svedberg says leaving S-E-Banken not tied to merge.
newsitem.headline: Svedberg says leaving S-E-Banken not tied to merge.

text.p: Managing director of Sweden's S-E-Banken, Bjorn Svedberg, said on Tuesday that his departure from the bank had nothing to do with the failed merger talks with Nordbanken.
S-E-Banken announced on Tuesday that Svedberg would leave his position at the annual general meeting on April 29 when his five year contract expires.
"My departure has no connection with the merger talks with Nordbanken," Svedberg told a news conference.
"But had it been that we had moved into a reshaping of the bank it is possible that I would have offered to stay on."
Merger talks between S-E-Banken and state-controlled Nordbanken collapsed earlier this year although many market players are speculating that talks will resume.
No clear reason was given for the failure but analysts suggested it was related to the proposed management structure or price.

Svedberg also said he would leave the bank's board and said it was with mixed feelings that he was leaving the bank. He will concentrate on his work with other industrial boards of which he is a member.
The bank said his deputy, Jacob Wallenberg, 41, was proposed as his successor.
Wallenberg is a member of the powerful Swedish financial family that controls around 18 percent of S-E-Banken.
